hints.title: Printer Turn Overlap Property
hints.text: A print operation can span an arbitrary range and cover previously printed characters. If the character at the start of a range matches a character inside, could they share the same stroke?

hints.title: Matching Boundary Optimization Reduction
hints.text: For substring [i, j], printing s[i] can optionally be extended to any index k where s[k] equals s[j], eliminating one independent turn.

hints.title: Subproblem Decomposition Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a table where dp[i][i] equals one turn. For range length from two to n, set dp[i][j] initially to dp[i][j - 1]. Check all intermediate split points k from i to j - 1. When s[k] matches s[j], subtract one from the sum of subproblem turns dp[i][k] and dp[k + 1][j]. Return dp[0][n - 1].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input size or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^3) time and O(N^2) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute-forcing all possible printer stroke sequences has exponential complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Interval DP tracks minimum turns for each substring in O(n^2) space and O(n^3) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand that matching end characters allow merging turns, leading to an interval DP subproblem.
